drivingQuestion: How can the verse say that the elders ate before God, when they ate before Moses?
outcomeNote: The difficulty in the verse is answered by the derasha, which restates the opening dictum as the verse's lesson.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין הַלֵּוִי: כׇּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִסְּעוּדָה שֶׁתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שָׁרוּי בְּתוֹכָהּ, כְּאִילּוּ נֶהֱנֶה מִזִּיו שְׁכִינָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיָּבֹא אַהֲרֹן וְכֹל זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֶאֱכׇל לֶחֶם עִם חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים״, וְכִי לִפְנֵי אֱלֹהִים אָכְלוּ? וַהֲלֹא לִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה אָכְלוּ!
segments.en: «And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said: One who partakes of a meal at which a Torah scholar is present, it is as if he enjoyed the radiant splendor of the Divine Presence, as it is stated: “And Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God”» (Exodus 18:12). «Did they» actually «eat before God? Didn’t they eat before Moses?»

segments.he: אֶלָּא לוֹמַר לָךְ כׇּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִסְּעוּדָה שֶׁתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שָׁרוּי בְּתוֹכָהּ — כְּאִילּוּ נֶהֱנֶה מִזִּיו שְׁכִינָה.
segments.en: «Rather,» this verse comes «to tell you» that «one who partakes in a meal at which a Torah scholar is present, it is as if he enjoyed the radiant splendor of the Divine Presence.»
